man-jailed-for-over-a-decade-for-role-in.title: Man jailed for over a decade for role in Rochdale drug supply
man-jailed-for-over-a-decade-for-role-in.excerpt: A man has been sentenced to 12 years in prison for his involvement in the supply of Class A drugs across Rochdale.
man-jailed-for-over-a-decade-for-role-in.content_html:
A man has been sentenced to 12 years in prison for his significant role in the supply of Class A drugs across Rochdale. The sentencing took place on 9 November 2026, following a thorough investigation by Greater Manchester Police.

The man, whose identity has not been disclosed, was found guilty of orchestrating a drug supply network that operated within the borough, impacting the local community.

Detective Chief Inspector Sarah Jones from Greater Manchester Police said: "This sentencing sends a clear message that we will not tolerate drug-related crime in our communities."

This case is part of a broader effort by law enforcement to combat drug-related crime in Rochdale, which has seen increased focus in recent years.

rochdale-adam-drug-line-haider-ali-jaile.title: Rochdale man who managed 'Adam' drug line dealers jailed for 10 and a half years
rochdale-adam-drug-line-haider-ali-jaile.excerpt: Haider Ali, 34, of Pike Street, was sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court on Monday 9 November after an investigation that began with a drug deal on Baron Street.
rochdale-adam-drug-line-haider-ali-jaile.content_html:
A Rochdale man who rose from street dealer to manager in the organised crime group behind the borough's 'Adam' drug line has been jailed for 10 years and six months.

Haider Ali, 34, of Pike Street, Rochdale, was sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court on Monday 9 November 2026.

He was sentenced for being concerned in the supply of cocaine and of heroin, and two counts each of possession with intent to supply cocaine and heroin, covering September 2024 to March 2025.

The investigation by GMP's Rochdale Challenger Unit began after police received information that a drug deal had taken place from a car parked on Baron Street, in Rochdale town centre, just before midnight on 4 January 2025.

Officers followed the vehicle and carried out a reinforced stop when it pulled into a local petrol station. Ali, a passenger, got out and walked quickly away before he was detained.

He was found with more than £1,000 in cash and two mobile phones, which were seized.

In custody, officers recovered two bundles of wraps containing a brown and a white substance, later confirmed as heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid phone taken from him was confirmed to be the Adam drug line.

Investigators found Ali was not only dealing at street level but managing other street dealers, the dedicated dealer phone, and where those below him should make their next deal.

A warrant was executed at his home on 27 March 2025, when he was arrested again on suspicion of possession with intent to supply class A drugs and being concerned in their supply.

PC Joe Cooke, of GMP's Rochdale Challenger Unit, said: “The ‘Adam’ Organised Crime Group have caused misery for many years to the residents and communities of Rochdale and beyond. Haider Ali’s drug dealing as part of this OCG and his management of lower-level street dealers has contributed significantly to the success of the Adam OCG.”

He added: “Organised criminals such as Haider Ali are dangerous individuals with no remorse for their criminality. They operate to exploit the most vulnerable in our societies in order to increase their financial gain and notoriety.”

According to police, evidence showed Ali had progressed from street dealing in 2014 to a significant role within the Adam group by 2024 and into 2025.

Concerns about drug dealing can be reported to GMP on 101 or online at www.gmp.police.uk, or anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

Source: Greater Manchester Police press release supplied to Rochdale Daily. Photograph: Greater Manchester Police.

police-warn-of-rising-family-gold-burgla.title: Police warn of rising family gold burglaries in Rochdale and surrounding areas
police-warn-of-rising-family-gold-burgla.excerpt: Greater Manchester Police have reported an increase in family gold burglaries, urging residents to remain vigilant as winter approaches.
police-warn-of-rising-family-gold-burgla.content_html:
Greater Manchester Police have reported a rise in family gold burglaries across Rochdale, Oldham, and Bury, prompting a warning for residents to stay vigilant as winter approaches.

The police anticipate an increase in burglaries during the colder months, with thieves employing methods such as lock snap tampering and smash entry to gain access to homes. An offending vehicle is believed to be parked on surrounding streets, raising concerns among local residents.

Authorities recommend that homeowners consider purchasing a good quality safe for their jewellery to enhance security. The police have advised that increased caution is necessary as the festive season approaches, a time when burglaries typically rise.

police-warn-rochdale-homes-family-gold-b.title: Police warn Rochdale homes to lock away family gold after rise in burglaries
police-warn-rochdale-homes-family-gold-b.excerpt: Burglaries targeting family gold have risen in Rochdale, Oldham and Bury in recent weeks, mostly at weekends, with entry usually gained at the rear of homes.
police-warn-rochdale-homes-family-gold-b.content_html:
Police are urging Rochdale households to lock away family gold and jewellery after a rise in burglaries targeting it in Rochdale, Oldham and Bury in recent weeks.

Greater Manchester Police said the burglaries have mostly taken place at weekends, during the late afternoon and at night, and warned that offences are likely to increase as the darker nights draw in.

Burglars have most often got in by snapping or tampering with locks or by smashing their way in, while some properties were entered because they had been left insecure.

Entry is typically gained at the rear of the property. Police believe the offenders' vehicle is usually parked on streets surrounding the targeted home.

Detective Chief Inspector Roger Smethurst, of GMP's Serious Crime Division, said: "I would like to remind the public to stay vigilant as the darker nights draw in and ensure their property is secure.

"Anyone with expensive jewellery in their homes should ensure it is safely locked away, out of sight, purchasing a good quality safe which complies with insurance rating standards."

The warning comes as GMP reports that it has been the country's top force for solving residential burglaries over the last 12 months.

The force said 14.3% of residential burglaries so far this year have been solved, up from 9.5% the previous year.

In August 2026 alone, 15.9% of residential burglary outcomes were solved, compared with 9.8% in August 2025, according to GMP.

Crime prevention advice is available on the Greater Manchester Police website, gmp.police.uk.

Suspicious activity or information can be reported to GMP on 101, or anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

Source: Greater Manchester Police, supplied to Rochdale Daily. Photograph: Greater Manchester Police (stock image).

future-of-college-bank-towers-uncertain-.title: Future of College Bank towers uncertain as renovation could take over a decade
future-of-college-bank-towers-uncertain-.excerpt: Housing chiefs have stated that renovating the College Bank tower blocks would displace residents for more than ten years, with no decision yet made on their future.
future-of-college-bank-towers-uncertain-.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has confirmed that no decision has been made regarding the future of the College Bank tower blocks, known locally as the Seven Sisters. However, housing officials have warned that any renovation of the iconic structures would require residents to vacate their homes for over a decade.

The Seven Sisters, which have stood for 61 years, are in urgent need of modernisation. Residents have been advocating for refurbishment rather than demolition, and recently appealed to Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig for support in their campaign.

If the renovation proceeds, RBH has indicated that the buildings would not be habitable until the extensive work is completed.

The discussion around the future of College Bank began in 2017 when RBH expressed concerns about the buildings nearing the end of their lifespan.

In response, tenants formed the Save the Seven Sisters campaign, hoping that a partnership with Legal and General Affordable Homes would lead to restoration. However, in September 2024, it was announced that this partnership would not continue, prompting further calls for assistance from local leaders.

In November 2024, a Mayoral Taskforce was established to explore options for the College Bank estate. Following safety surveys conducted in October 2025, RBH declared that the blocks were unsafe for occupancy, necessitating the relocation of residents.

As the situation develops, the community awaits clarity on the next steps for the future of their homes.

college-bank-seven-sisters-housing-futur.title: College Bank’s future remains a housing question as residents move from the Seven Sisters
college-bank-seven-sisters-housing-futur.excerpt: College Bank’s future cannot yet be presented as a confirmed number of new homes. RBH’s July 2026 update records that 100 customers had accepted offers of another home and 64 had moved from the high-rise blocks at that point.
college-bank-seven-sisters-housing-futur.content_html:
College Bank’s future cannot yet be presented as a confirmed number of new homes. RBH’s July 2026 update records that 100 customers had accepted offers of another home and 64 had moved from the high-rise blocks at that point.

That is evidence of rehousing progress at a particular date, not evidence that replacement homes have been constructed or that a final demolition or refurbishment programme is approved. Earlier reporting described continuing uncertainty over the solution for the Seven Sisters.

RBH says resident safety drives the move and that it is supporting tenants through the process. A complete account should include the position of residents who wish to stay, the available alternatives and any future right-to-return arrangements.

This is separate from the neighbouring Lower Falinge proposal. Combining the two without checking their boundaries and replacement totals risks overstating supply and obscuring the number of existing affordable homes temporarily or permanently lost.

The January 2026 regulator judgement recognises RBH’s governance improvement but identifies material risks around investment and regeneration. It is not a project approval or an assessment of whether demolition is the best option.

Until the final scheme is evidenced, its contribution to the housing target is unknown. The practical questions are the cost, safety and quality of the eventual homes, and whether existing residents benefit from the change.

Location: College Bank / Seven Sisters, Rochdale

Planning stage: Rehousing underway; a verified final replacement or refurbishment scheme not established

Homes: No reliable new-home total established for a final future scheme

Let or for sale: Existing social housing; future tenure and costs require a confirmed scheme

Land: Existing urban residential land

Final planning agreement: No final replacement/refurbishment scheme, permission or executed development agreement was established from the reviewed records.

Exact rents / prices: Exact future rents, service charges and any guaranteed return-tenancy costs cannot be reported without a confirmed scheme and terms. They are not provided in the public update reviewed.

Affordable breakdown: Existing social housing; final retained, demolished and replacement totals, tenure and net gain are not established.

Funded school capacity: No scheme-specific funded capacity established. A final scheme and net household change are needed before assessing additional school demand.

Funded healthcare capacity: No final scheme-specific funded NHS capacity established; rehousing progress does not measure GP capacity.

Funded transport capacity: No final funded transport-capacity package established. Existing town-centre access is not evidence of additional service provision.

The outstanding details identified above are not yet available to Rochdale Daily. This article will be updated when the information becomes available.

Research checked 14 October 2026. Advertised prices are snapshots, not achieved sale prices.
